subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finbot.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@finbot.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Alex / Sana —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our 30m discovery so we’re all aligned and so Ben and I can scope a concrete pilot. High-level notes below and next steps at the bottom.

Pain points you highlighted
- Unit economics are the biggest blocker: inference cost per active user is eroding margins for your core summarization product.
- Current throughput constraints: you have spiky traffic (~200 QPS peak) but small average batch sizes due to a low P95 latency requirement.
- Caching not yet implemented for prompts with repeating prefixes (templates + system messages), and KV-cache reuse is minimal across requests.
- Concern about quantization: willing to explore but nervous about any quality degradation for customer-facing summaries.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Primary model: managed 13B open model via third-party API (8k context).
- Serving: single-region managed endpoints with basic autoscaling; no internal dedicated GPU fleet.
- Observability: request-level latency + token counts, but no token-level cost bucketing per route.

Success criteria you named
- Reduce inference cost per 1M tokens by ~40–60% while keeping p95 latency under ~300ms for production queries.
- Preserve summary quality within a ~2% tolerance vs. current baseline as measured by the eval set.
- Pilot must be limited-scope (QA/canary) before ramping to prod.

What Redwood can do / initial suggestions
- Unit-econ analysis: attached spreadsheet with conservative/optimistic scenarios showing batching, KV caching, and 4-bit quantization estimates.
- Batching & latency controls: we can configure continuous batching with latency SLOs so small batches don’t cause unacceptable tail latency.
- KV/prefix caching: quick wins if you have templated prompts — we expect 15–35% token savings depending on reuse.
- Quantization experiment: agreed path is to run an A/B on a subset of traffic (QA -> canary) and run eval regressions. We’ll provide recommended quant profiles.

Open items / asks from your side
- Share a representative sample of queries (anonymized) or a small eval set so we can run quality checks against quantized variants.
- Confirm internal success metric: is cost per active user the primary KPI or token-level cost?
- Any compliance/SOC2 constraints that would affect a private deployment pilot? (Sana mentioned SOC2 scope may be relevant)

Next steps
1) Marissa to share the unit-econ spreadsheet + pilot proposal (attached). — today (attached: redwood_unit_econ_estimate.xlsx)
2) Ben to coordinate a technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer to map integration points — propose 60m next week.
3) Alex/Sana to share a small anonymized eval set and confirm compliance constraints (SOC2 scoping).
4) Align on a 2-week pilot plan (QA -> canary) and success gates.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_unit_econ_estimate.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)], [Attachment: SOC2-summary-2025.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep-dive pending your availability.

Best,
Marissa

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finbot.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Sana Patel <sana.patel@finbot.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the thorough write-up. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- The primary KPI we’re optimizing for is cost per MAU, but engineering also needs token-level cost transparency for forecasting. So both are important; if you can surface both in the pilot that would be ideal.
- We’re definitely open to batching but the critical constraint is p95 latency for interactive summaries — can you share expected p95 delta at different batching timeouts? Even ballpark numbers will help.
- Quantization: we’re open to trying 4-bit/8-bit in QA, but we need a clear regression test. Can Redwood run your quantized model variants against our small eval set and return BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics + a blind human check on ~50 examples?
- Compliance: Sana — I’ll sync with you on SOC2 items. For pilot we need to know if S3 staging is acceptable or if we need to run in our VPC.

On next steps: we can share a 500-example anonymized eval set by Friday and have our infra lead join the deep-dive. Proposed deep-dive times: Mon 3/1 10am PT or Tue 3/2 2pm PT — either works for us.

Thanks — looking forward to the spreadsheet.

—Alex
Alex Rivera | Head of ML Infrastructure, FinBot
alex.rivera@finbot.com | +1 (617) 555-0199
